correctness.rationale: Positive two-cycle equations yield v-y=(x-u)(1-1/x-1/u) and x+u<2lambda-2<=4, so 1/x+1/u>1. Monotone h and h(x)h(u)=1 force the opposite sign when x!=u, hence only fixed points. At each lambda>3, z between 2 and min(lambda-1,(lambda+3)/3) enables small-epsilon positive orbit construction; limit intercept lies strictly in (0,1) and slope positive. The rational lambda=4 orbit and three other points were independently checked with exact Fraction arithmetic. No finite check substitutes for analytical quantifiers.

value.rationale: The exact lambda=3 boundary yields a strong global constraint on genuine positive two-cycles for any nondecreasing predator response, including the current discrete ecology model, and is sharp with strict positive affine parameters above the boundary. The result discriminates logistic period doubling from coexisting predator-prey two-cycles and supports precise questions about higher-period dynamics; it is not a merely numerical parameter sample or a renamed special case.
